owner: Existing Reading Activity canonical domain and ObsidianService/SyncQueueService; pure ReadingTransportBinding/Request/Entry/Response never persist or authenticate
wire_encoding: UTF-8 without BOM; compact JSON using the declared key order. No duplicate keys, trailing bytes, alternate number encodings, raw CR/LF in lines or lone Unicode surrogates. UTC timestamps use the existing Dart canonical 3-or-6 fractional-digit convention. No credentials or private paths in payloads.
binding: Opaque pairing generation, vault scope, device and source DB epoch must match the current authenticated principal. Rotate/revoke pairing on account/vault/credential changes. Fields are public context, never credentials or authority. Parsing alone authenticates nothing.
batch_id: qrtb_ + lowercase SHA-256 of compact UTF-8 JSON [quartzo-reading-transport-batch-v1, binding_id, vault_scope, device_id, source_epoch, event_lines]. Fresh retries keep immutable event_lines and batch ID; native IDs still deduplicate regrouped batches.
request_id: qrtr_ + fresh 128-bit lowercase hexadecimal nonce for each attempt. Require explicit UTC now, issued_at <= now < expires_at and lifetime <=300 seconds. The nonce binds the response; persisted replay/idempotency enforcement by an authenticated receiver remains required.
event_lines: Each is one existing canonical ReadingActivityEvent JSON object, without LF. Keeping exact bounded strings permits independent malformed/unsupported-event rejection without hiding valid neighbors. Outbox preserves each line before transmission. Inspect all entries before commit; same native ID with divergent payload quarantines every matching entry in that request.
result_binding: Exactly one ordered result for every input position, with SHA-256 of that exact UTF-8 line. Eligible event_id and native_digest must match local recomputation. Invalid/unsupported/conflicting entries have null event_id/native_digest and cannot claim committed/duplicate. Native digest hashes existing nativePayload excluding observation time.
canonical_commit: Only committed/duplicate may carry an opaque nonempty canonical commit revision, after the authenticated canonical owner has proven persistence; duplicate also requires a proven existing canonical native payload. Other outcomes require null. Merely supplying a revision string or matching an echo never proves durability.
ack_boundary: Response decoder exposes untrusted claims only. It has no accepted-event/cursor grant or receipt issuer. No ReadingLocalCommit, scratch index, diagnostic receipt, staged result, queue insertion or uploaded byte result can mint a canonical ACK. A future authenticated protocol owner must verify durable canonical receipts and persist outbox acknowledgements per event; request order is never a source watermark.
remaining: Authenticated production transport selection and credential lifecycle
Canonical cross-process/Drive/Companion durability and receipt issuer
Persistent replay/idempotency and native conflict checks across batches
PW3 offline/reboot/cancellation/lost-ACK and real canonical persistence tests
